audit.whatIsWrong: report[14].t quotes 45.48%; the packet says 49.11% over 615 games.
audit.why: One number from the packet — and this is the largest sample in my slice, so the figure carries weight.
Lucian owns 1 through 6, even at first item, Yi at 2+. Chart matches the packet and both layers agree row for row.
audit.corrected: No change to the level chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four places describe Lucian as having 'two E-charges', a 'double E-dash' or a 'double-dash'. Relentless Pursuit is a single dash on 16/15.5/15/14.5/14s.
audit.why: The real mechanic is better and different: Lightslinger attacks reduce Relentless Pursuit's cooldown, so he refunds his dash by landing double-shots on you. That makes denying his autos the way to keep his escape down — an actionable rule the phantom second charge replaced with fatalism.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why, breakdown.mid, breakdown.cooldowns, spikes[3].text and content.mid rewritten around the 16s cooldown and the Lightslinger refund.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never states that Piercing Light is only 500 range, shorter than Alpha Strike's 600.
audit.why: It is the one range comparison in Yi's favour in an otherwise losing lane — his poke does not out-reach your blink, his autos and W do. It changes where you stand to farm.
audit.corrected: Written into report[5].t alongside the dash-refund interaction.

audit.whatIsWrong: The missing-interactions file asserts 'Lucian sustains through chip damage (Lightslinger)' and calls for Grievous Wounds timing.
audit.why: Riot's passive text has no self-healing: it triggers when Lucian is healed or shielded BY AN ALLY, or when a nearby enemy is immobilized. The heal and shield flags on the passive are tooltip-parsing misfires. I did not write anti-heal advice into the page on the strength of them.
audit.corrected: No edit made. Recorded so the flag is not trusted on the next pass.

edits.before: Highlander's slow immunity helps you dodge ganks and stick briefly, but Lucian's E plus double E-dash spacing still kites your one engage.
edits.after: Highlander's 85s of speed helps you stick, but Relentless Pursuit refunds cooldown off his Lightslinger shots, so the dash returns before you do.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 stabilize slightly: Wuju Style's true damage and Meditate's sustain let you heal poke and take a short trade if Lucian whiffs an E. Level 6 Highlander is your first real tool — slow immunity to dodge ganks and a brief stick window — but Lucian's two E-charges still kite your single gap-close.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 stabilize: Wuju Style's true damage and Meditate's sustain heal the poke and let you trade if Lucian whiffs an E. Level 6 Highlander is your first real tool — slow immunity against ganks and a brief stick window — but his Lightslinger shots refund Relentless Pursuit, so the one dash keeps returning.

edits.before: Track Lucian's E (Relentless Pursuit) above all — it's both his escape from your Alpha Strike and his gap-close to poke. When E is down is your only safe window to walk up or all-in.
edits.after: Track Relentless Pursuit (E) above all — 16s at rank 1, but every Lightslinger double-shot he lands cuts it, so denying his autos is how you keep his escape down.

edits.before: Alpha Strike makes you untargetable to dodge his Q-pass and ganks, but his E (Relentless Pursuit) dash cancels your gap-close; Wuju Style adds true damage to beat any armor he buys; Meditate out-sustains his W/passive poke; Highlander's slow immunity ignores any slow from his items.
edits.after: Alpha Strike dodges Piercing Light, which reaches only 500 against your 600 blink — his autos and W are what out-range you. Relentless Pursuit answers the gap-close and his Lightslinger shots refund it; Wuju Style's true damage beats any armour he buys, and Meditate out-sustains the poke between his cooldowns.

edits.before: HARD (45.48% WR) — a textbook ranged-kiter-vs-Yi lane you lose early and must scale out of; survive to 2+ items and you flip it, but most games are decided before you get there.
edits.after: HARD (49.11% WR) — a textbook ranged-kiter-vs-Yi lane you lose early and must scale out of; survive to 2+ items and you flip it, but most games are decided before you get there.

edits.before: You out-scale — Highlander (R) resets and Alpha Strike (Q) dodges let you all-in a squishy Lucian, but respect that his double-dash and Culling (R) can still kite you if E is up when you commit.
edits.after: You out-scale — Highlander (R) resets and Alpha Strike (Q) dodges let you all-in a squishy Lucian, but his single dash returns fast off Lightslinger, so commit while Relentless Pursuit is spent.

edits.before: Even at 6 he holds the edge: his Culling (R) burst and double-dash out-damage your all-in, though you can Alpha Strike (Q) to break his ult lock — until you have items, respect his kill threat and farm.
edits.after: Even at 6 he holds the edge: The Culling (R) on 110s plus a dash he refunds off Lightslinger out-damages your all-in — until you have items, respect his kill threat and just farm the wave.

notes: Corrected a mechanic repeated four times: Lucian has one dash, not two charges. The real interaction is that Lightslinger attacks refund Relentless Pursuit's 16s, which makes denying his double-shots the way to keep his escape down. Also noted that Piercing Light is 500 range against Alpha Strike's 600 — the only range comparison in Yi's favour here. Win rate corrected from 45.48% to 49.11%. Left the Culling channel/target-lock claims alone: I could not verify from Riot's text whether Alpha Strike breaks it, and it is listed in unverified.
